code.originalText: Three-month review: A1c, urine albumin, lipids, eyes after laser treatment, heart, legs, grief, and a GLP-1 receptor agonist

text.paragraph: Three-month review: A1c, urine albumin, lipids, eyes after laser treatment, heart, legs, grief, and a GLP-1 receptor agonist. [S]

Mr. Robinson returns three months after his first visit. He had the third injections in both eyes a month ago and laser treatment to the right eye nearly three weeks ago. Dr. Ostrowski-Lane reports that the blood has largely cleared, the new vessels are regressing, the macular swelling is much less (central subfield 318 microns right and 334 left at the last scan), and his acuity has improved to 52 letters right and 68 left; she judges the retina stable enough to start a GLP-1 receptor agonist at a low dose with monthly review. The low-vision visit gave him magnifiers and better lighting. He walks two and a half blocks before calf pain in the exercise program. No chest pain. No low blood sugar. His PSA, HIV and hepatitis C tests were normal. He says the counseling helps and he sleeps better, though the loss is with him every day. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1971-10-26; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; blood pressure 126/76, pulse 60; weight 101.4 kg
Heel healed; no new breaks; fitted shoes

Blurred vision in both eyes, worse over two months, with new floaters in the right eye for four days; acuity by Snellen chart 20/200 right and 20/80 left; undilated view poor on the right; urgent retina examination arranged
S — Synthetic presenting finding, superseded by the retinal diagnosis two days later.
Tightness in the chest on climbing stairs for two months, easing with rest; ECG without acute change; cardiology evaluation with a stress test arranged
S — Synthetic presenting finding, superseded by the coronary diagnosis after the stress test.
Type 2 diabetes for about fifteen years, on metformin and basal insulin, with hyperglycemia (A1c 10.4%)
S — Synthetic modern episode linked to his documented diabetes.
Proliferative diabetic retinopathy in both eyes with center-involving diabetic macular edema (central subfield 412 microns right, 468 left); best-corrected acuity 35 letters right and 56 letters left
S — Synthetic retinal findings anchored to his documented loss of vision.
Vitreous hemorrhage in the right eye from proliferative retinopathy; retina attached on ultrasound
Hypertension with chronic kidney disease, above goal on lisinopril 20 mg (152/92 mmHg)
S — Synthetic modern episode linked to his documented high blood pressure.
Diabetic kidney disease with albuminuria (urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio 86 mg/g, also raised last year) and eGFR 79
Peripheral artery disease of both legs with calf pain after about one block of walking; faint foot pulses
S — Synthetic modern episode linked to the documented artery damage in his legs.
Diabetic peripheral neuropathy: loss of protective sensation in both feet on monofilament testing
S — Synthetic modern episode linked to the documented nerve damage in his legs.
History of two mild strokes a year ago, without lasting weakness
S — Synthetic modern coding of the documented strokes.
Hyperlipidemia: LDL 142 mg/dL on atorvastatin 40 mg, far above the goal below 55 mg/dL
Bereavement: his eldest son died in a car crash six weeks ago
S — Synthetic modern coding of a documented loss; grief is treated as grief, not as a disorder.

Coronary artery disease with stable angina on climbing stairs: a small reversible inferior perfusion defect on regadenoson stress imaging, ejection fraction 56%; medical therapy chosen with cardiology
S — Synthetic coronary diagnosis anchored to his documented heart disease; no heart attack is recorded before the episode.
Friction blister of the right heel from new shoes, unroofed, 2.5 by 2 cm, clean base, without infection, in a neuropathic foot with peripheral artery disease
S — Synthetic intercurrent problem at an unscheduled visit; it does not echo a documented event.

Retina clinic monthly, with injections extended as the swelling allows and laser to the left eye if new vessels persist.

Continue lisinopril 40 mg and empagliflozin.

Continue counseling; PHQ-9 again in six months or sooner if he wishes.

Follow-up: Retina clinic monthly. Lipids in four to eight weeks. Hepatitis B dose 2 in one month. Colonoscopy next month with the written preparation plan. Review in three months with the A1c. Call for nausea or vomiting that stops him drinking, any change in vision, chest pain, or a skin break on the feet. [S]
